# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a live textbook on how mechanisms carry and process information about the world:
how much a robot's body holds about its environment, how that depends on its design, and
how the information spreads through the body and is lost on the way. The environment
includes the forces acting on the body, and also properties such as the stiffness of the
ground, the shape of the terrain or the mass of a load. The results so far are about
contact forces, the running example. It starts from
@patterson2026quantifying, which compared actuator transmissions in legged robots with
information-theoretic measures, and it grows as new results come in.

## How the book is organized

Part I builds the main tool, the *energy metric*. It explains why the body's state is
measured in units of energy before noise is added, proves what that buys (invariance
under any change of coordinates, the right behaviour when a spring becomes rigid, results
that do not depend on a finite-element mesh), and works through the leg designs of the
running example. Part II asks whether energy is the right choice: it proves that energy
is the only noise model with a short list of physical properties, compares the
alternatives, and builds a thermally consistent body in which every design holds the same total and
designs differ in which parts of the body hold it. The research log holds dated notes,
the roadmap and the changelog.

## How the book changes

The book is not planned in advance. New results first appear as dated research notes in
the research log. A note moves into a chapter once its result is checked, its proofs are
labelled, and it connects to the existing material; the note stays as the dated record.
The [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) lists the open threads and what happens next on each, and the
[changelog](CHANGELOG.md) lists what changed in each release.

Every page opens with its status:

- *exploratory*: a new result, checked by code but not yet connected to the rest;
- *draft*: connected and proved, still being revised;
- *stable*: unlikely to change except for corrections.

## What you can rely on

Every number in the text is computed by the Python package `mibook` in this book's
repository, and a test in `tests/` pins it, so a number that drifts fails the build.
Figures are generated by code cells when the book is built. A proof that is not complete
is titled "Proof sketch" and says what it assumes. Every citation is marked by whether
its source was read in full or only through abstracts and citing works
(@sec-sources).

## Reproducing the book

The repository is [github.com/CyPhiLab/mechintelligence](https://github.com/CyPhiLab/mechintelligence).
With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed:

```bash
uv sync
uv run pytest
uv run quarto render
```

The computations depend on the analysis library from
[zpatty/quadruped-mech-info](https://github.com/zpatty/quadruped-mech-info), pinned to
a fixed commit.

## How to cite

Cite the version you read, since pages change between releases:

> Patterson, Z. J. *Mechanical Intelligence: A live textbook on information in
> mechanisms.* Version 0.1, 2026. <https://mechintelligence.cyphilab.com/>
